explain.say: The poem opens with one word: Hwaet! It means something like Listen! A singer is calling a noisy hall to silence. Beowulf was composed in Old English, perhaps in the 700s or later, and survives in one manuscript copied around the year 1000. The panels tell Beowulf's three great fights.

explain.say: Now listen to how the poet talks. He calls the sea the whale-road. That is a kenning, two words squeezed into a picture for one thing, as the board shows. Each line splits in two halves, tied by words starting with the same sound. Can you invent a kenning for your phone?

explain.say: The heroic code holds this world together: a lord gives treasure, his warriors give loyalty to the death, and fame is the only thing that lasts. Look at the fifth panel. When old Beowulf fights the dragon, his men flee into the woods. Only young Wiglaf stays. What does that say about the code?

explain.say: The last panel: Beowulf dies, is burned on a pyre and buried in a great mound by the sea, while his people fear the future. In 1936 J. R. R. Tolkien argued the monsters are the heart of the poem, not a distraction. Wonderful work. Challenge: is Beowulf's last fight brave, or proud?

faq.q: Why does Beowulf fight Grendel without a sword?
faq.a: Grendel uses no weapons, so Beowulf chooses a fair fight for greater glory. The poem later reveals that ordinary blades could not have harmed Grendel anyway.

faq.q: Why does only Wiglaf help Beowulf against the dragon?
faq.a: The other chosen warriors panic and flee into the woods. Wiglaf remembers the gifts Beowulf gave them and the loyalty they owe, so he stays and helps kill the dragon.
asks: Who helps Beowulf fight the dragon?

faq.a: Beowulf kills the dragon with Wiglaf's help but is fatally wounded. He is burned on a pyre and buried in a mound on a headland, and his people mourn and fear the attacks to come.
asks: What happens at the end of Beowulf?

faq.a: A compressed metaphor, usually two words joined, used instead of a plain noun: whale-road for the sea, bone-house for the body. Old English poetry is full of them.

faq.q: What did Tolkien say about Beowulf?
faq.a: In his 1936 lecture The Monsters and the Critics, Tolkien argued that the monsters are central to the poem's meaning, and that it should be read as a poem, not just as history.

facts: Beowulf survives in a single manuscript, Cotton Vitellius A.xv, in the British Library.
The manuscript was damaged in the Ashburnham House fire of 1731.
The poem is about 3,180 lines long.
